Every morning, clicking on that devotional and listening to what was written for the day has changed me. Maybe not in all 31 days because I started a little late more like 29 but something in me shifted deeply in that short amount of time. I live in Texas so the live devotional didn’t air until 11 AM and I would listen, but I was already midway into my day by then, however before I would get out of my bed, opening the app and reading or having my phone read the devotional to me (since you know faith comes by hearing) has truly been a blessing and “unlocked” is now part of my vocabulary & my experience. 

I’ve been a born-again Christian for most of my 50 years on this earth. I grew up in church. I’ve loved God for as long as I can remember. But through this devotional series, I learned more about the God I’ve served my whole life in 30 days than I did in 40+ years sitting in church pews.

For the first time, I truly began understanding my identity in Christ not just emotionally, but biblically. I received practical instruction on how we are supposed to operate as believers in a way I had honestly never fully grasped before.

It has changed how I speak to my children, my nieces, my nephews, and even how I counsel people around me. One of the biggest things that stayed with me is this: Word first. Feelings lie. Feelings are not facts. Get information.

Turning to the Word first thing in the morning has transformed my days. Even reading scripture now feels different. There’s a level of understanding and enjoyment that simply did not exist for me before. I find myself reading a chapter and literally saying out loud, “Wow… it’s right there. It’s been right there the whole time.”

I’m incredibly grateful.

And I know people in my circle are probably tired of hearing me say, “I was listening to Pastor Johnny Chang…” but I’m going to keep saying it not to glorify a man, but to highlight a mission that is clearly helping people reconnect with God through truth and clarity.

What’s been revealed to me in such a short time about something I’ve known my entire life is honestly overwhelming in the best way.
